AI Security, Privacy & Forensics

Investigating how intelligent systems expose information, fail under attack, and leave evidence that can be examined.

Research Description

Overview

What can AI systems reveal, what can be manipulated, and what evidence survives? We study these questions across writing and voice assistants, generative editing tools, wearables, and other connected devices. Our work spans text, audio, images, video, and sensor signals in systems that use large language models (LLMs) and vision–language models (VLMs).

Research Thrusts

Adversarial integrity across modalities

We study how manipulated inputs affect what AI systems infer, including when wearable signals and their text descriptions disagree.

Privacy in consumer AI and devices

We examine what AI tools can infer about people from ordinary writing or speech, and whether editing tools can reduce unwanted inference without changing what users mean.

Forensic evidence and provenance

We evaluate which traces remain after an AI edit or application interaction and what those traces can establish about the change or activity.

Research Goals

Develop reproducible methods to test the integrity of multimodal AI, measure sensitive-attribute inference, and recover and interpret forensic evidence.

Intellectual Merit

Connect what people do in an AI application, what models infer from that activity, and what evidence remains on a device or in the content.

Research Impact

The work helps researchers and practitioners evaluate privacy protections, test sensing systems, and assess the origin and integrity of digital evidence.

Selected Studies

Preprint

Wearable AI across the lifecycle

Sensor data→Integrity checks→Reliable interpretation

Wearable learning pipelines turn time-varying measurements into activity and wellbeing inferences. Changes to training signals, labels or cross-modal alignment can affect both predictive behavior and the trustworthiness of subsequent explanations.

Research objectives

Study data integrity, poisoning detection and sanitization while evaluating whether useful activity information is retained.

Approach & Intellectual Merit

We study wearable sensor data, activity labels, and the alignment between signals and text. The selected study evaluates large language models for detecting and sanitizing corrupted training data.

Selected publications

Adaptive and Robust Data Poisoning Detection and Sanitization in Wearable IoT Systems using Large Language Models ↗

Research Relevance

For wearable activity recognition, we evaluate detection, localization, and recovery separately, including whether cleaned data still retain useful activity information.

ACL 2026 Industry Track

Privacy in human–AI interaction

Text / audio→Consumer AI transformation→Privacy ↔ utility

Everyday writing and audio-editing tools may reveal sensitive attributes, but may also help transform content to reduce unwanted inference. The same consumer interface can therefore act as both a privacy risk and a possible defense.

Research objectives

Measure how transformations affect sensitive-attribute inference while preserving the usefulness and meaning of the original content.

Approach & Intellectual Merit

We compare original and edited content to measure how consumer AI transformations affect what other models can infer.

Selected publications

No Innocence in Styling: Discovery of Privacy Protection Capabilities and Security Risks in Consumer Generative AI Writing Assistants ↗

Research Relevance

For writing and audio tools, we compare privacy and utility together: did editing reduce sensitive-attribute inference, and did it preserve meaning?

EMNLP 2026

On-device generative image-edit forensics

Consumer image edit→Detect & localize→Provenance evidence

Consumer editing tools can alter a localized part of an image while leaving most of the scene intact. Detecting these changes requires attention to real device workflows, not only to images generated entirely from scratch.

Research objectives

Detect and localize consumer-tool edits, evaluate multilingual edit descriptions and examine the effects of compression.

Approach & Intellectual Merit

The published Edits in the Wild work introduces ConsumerGenEdit as a benchmark grounded in consumer platforms. Its intellectual contribution is an evaluation setting that links localized edits, platform conditions and language-based descriptions.

Selected publications

Edits in the Wild: A Multilingual Benchmark for Localizing On-Device Generative Image Edits on Consumer Platforms ↗

Research Relevance

The benchmark supports provenance and fact-checking research by showing where an image changed. Localizing an edit cannot establish intent or reconstruct the full editing history.

Preprint

AI application forensics

Application activity→Recoverable artifacts→Qualified interpretation

AI applications leave digital traces beyond their visible conversations. Understanding which artifacts persist, and what they can legitimately establish, is important for reproducible examination of emerging interfaces.

Research objectives

Identify and characterize traces associated with the ChatGPT Windows application and their interpretation in forensic research.

Approach & Intellectual Merit

The study documents artifacts that remain outside the visible chat interface.

Selected publications

Digital Forensic Investigation of the ChatGPT Windows Application ↗

Research Relevance

For forensic examination, we distinguish traces the application leaves from conclusions about what a user did, and consider how versions and settings affect which artifacts remain.
